question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y=9 \cos{\left(u \right)},\qquad u=\sin{\left(x \right)}.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=- 9 \sin{\left(u \right)},\qquad \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\cos{\left(x \right)}.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} &=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\ &=(- 9 \sin{\left(u \right)})\cdot (\cos{\left(x \right)}) \\ &=- 9 \sin{\left(\sin{\left(x \right)} \right)} \cos{\left(x \right)}.\end{aligned}
$$

y=\operatorname{sec}⁡(u),\,u=\operatorname{csc}⁡(x).

$$

 \dfrac{\textrm d f}{\textrm d x} &= \dfrac{\textrm d f}{\textrm d u} \cdot \dfrac{\textrm d u}{\textrm d x}\\
